methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Shinkei, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Saif Khawaja and Reed Ginsberg, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), with particular focus on five leading peers including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Locus Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, using total capital raised as a proxy base value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Series A to the next funding round, implying a $60M valuation. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Walden Robotics at $1.1B (Seed stage). The peer median of $1.6B reflects the trajectory of funded robotics companies in this market.

These methods triangulate to a wide range of $51M to $1.9B, with a median implied valuation of $855M. The substantial spread reflects meaningful uncertainty in stage-appropriate valuation within the robotics sector. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods suggests either that Shinkei's capital efficiency or market position differs materially from peers, or that peer comparables span broader operational maturity than Shinkei's current stage. Further diligence on product-market fit, runway, and unit economics would narrow this range.
